# Vlocalhost AI

> An on-device AI meeting notetaker. It records, transcribes and summarises
> meetings entirely on the user's own machine. No bot joins the call and no
> audio is uploaded. Free forever for individual use, open source under
> AGPL-3.0, for Windows and macOS.

**Not to be confused with `localhost`.** "Vlocalhost" is a product name, not a
typo for the loopback hostname. The site is vlocal.host.

## What it is

Vlocalhost AI captures the audio your computer can already hear, so nothing
joins the meeting as a participant. A voice-activity gate discards silence,
a local Whisper model turns speech into text, and a local Ollama model writes
the summary. The transcript and the summary are written to the user's own disk
as plain text files. There is no account, no server, and no telemetry.

The only outbound request the application can make is a version check, and it
runs only when a person presses "Check for updates". It sends no identifier and
not even the installed version number.

## Who it is for

- People whose employer blocks meeting bots. Microsoft Teams shipped tenant-wide
  automatic blocking of external AI notetakers in August 2026, and universities
  publish named block lists.
- Regulated work — clinics, law firms, advisers, small public bodies — where a
  recording leaving the machine is a compliance question rather than a setting.
- Anyone who does not want a vendor holding an archive of their conversations.

## How it compares

- Against cloud notetakers (Otter, Fireflies, Granola): those upload the audio
  to be transcribed and summarised. Vlocalhost does neither. Some of them no
  longer send a bot into the call, which is a different thing from not
  uploading.
- Against other local notetakers (Meetily, Talat, Screenpipe): the architecture
  is comparable and honestly so. Vlocalhost differs on shipped calendar and
  mailbox integration, and on fleet model management for teams.

Privacy is the entry ticket to this category, not the differentiator within it.

## Pricing

- **Solo — $0, forever.** Unlimited on-device recording, transcription and
  summaries. This is the whole product for one person, not a trial.
- Pro, Team and Enterprise are announced but **not released**. Nothing is behind
  a paywall today.

## Files it produces

Every meeting writes two plain-text files into the user's own notes folder:

- `<date>_<title>-transcript.txt` — the full record, every line timestamped
- `<date>_<title>-summary.txt` — Summary, Key Discussion Points, Decisions and
  Action Items, with no timestamps

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 or macOS. A Linux build exists on the release but is not yet
  advertised as supported.
- [Ollama](https://ollama.com) running locally for summaries. Recording and
  transcription work without it; only the summary step needs it.
- No GPU required. A local model means summarising a long meeting takes on the
  order of a minute or two rather than seconds.
